name: Curtain Up
subject: Broadway and musicals
tagline: Twenty questions on show tunes, long runs and the people behind the footlights. Starts easy, ends hard.

questions.q: Who wrote and starred in Hamilton, the hip-hop musical about America's first treasury secretary?
questions.w: Lin-Manuel Miranda, who got the idea reading Ron Chernow's biography on holiday.
questions.more: He performed the opening number at the White House in 2009, six years before the show opened, and the audience laughed at the idea of a Hamilton rap. It won eleven Tony Awards and the Pulitzer Prize for Drama. Miranda left the cast in 2016; the filmed version with the original company reached Disney+ in 2020.

questions.q: 'Defying Gravity' is the big first-act finale of which musical?
questions.w: Wicked, the back story of the witches of Oz, which opened on Broadway in 2003.
questions.more: Based on Gregory Maguire's novel, it reframes the Wicked Witch of the West as a misunderstood green girl named Elphaba, after L. Frank Baum's initials. Critics were lukewarm but audiences were not, and it has grossed more than five billion dollars worldwide. The two-part film arrived in 2024 and 2025.

questions.q: Who composed The Phantom of the Opera, Cats and Evita?
questions.w: Andrew Lloyd Webber, the British composer who at one point had six shows running on Broadway at once.
questions.more: He wrote Phantom for his then wife Sarah Brightman, who played Christine. Lloyd Webber is one of very few people to have won an Emmy, a Grammy, an Oscar and a Tony, and he sits in the House of Lords. His father was a church organist and his brother Julian is a concert cellist.

questions.q: The musical Cats is based on a book of poems by which writer?
questions.w: T. S. Eliot, whose Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats was written for his godchildren in 1939.
questions.more: Eliot's widow Valerie gave Lloyd Webber an unpublished fragment about Grizabella, the faded glamour cat, which became the show's one real story and its hit, 'Memory'. Cats ran for 21 years in London and 18 on Broadway. The 2019 film was a famous catastrophe.

questions.q: 'Don't Cry for Me Argentina' is sung by the title character of which musical?
questions.w: Evita, about Eva Perón, the actress who became first lady of Argentina.
questions.more: Lloyd Webber and Tim Rice released it as a concept album in 1976 before anyone staged it, and the song was a British number one for Julie Covington. Elaine Paige, Patti LuPone and Madonna have all played Eva; Madonna wrote to the director to get the film role and won a Golden Globe for it.

questions.q: Which Disney musical, with its animal puppets and masks, is the highest-grossing Broadway show of all time?
questions.w: The Lion King, which opened in 1997 and has taken more than two billion dollars on Broadway alone.
questions.more: The director Julie Taymor put the actors' faces in full view beneath the animal masks, and became the first woman to win the Tony for directing a musical. The opening procession of animals down the aisles still draws gasps. Worldwide it has outgrossed every film and album in history.

questions.q: True or false: to count as a 'Broadway' theatre, a New York playhouse must have at least 500 seats.
questions.w: True. Off-Broadway houses seat 100 to 499; Off-Off-Broadway fewer than 100.
questions.more: Only four of the 41 Broadway theatres actually sit on the street called Broadway; the rest are on the side streets of the Theater District around Times Square. The oldest still in use, the Lyceum and the New Amsterdam, opened in 1903. On Broadway the lights are dimmed for a minute when a theatre great dies.

questions.q: Which show holds the record as the longest-running in Broadway history, with 13,981 performances before it closed in 2023?
questions.w: The Phantom of the Opera, which ran for 35 years at the Majestic Theatre.
questions.more: Its chandelier crash was engineered to drop at the end of the first act eight times a week without ever hurting anyone. The closing was announced during the slow recovery from the pandemic, and ticket demand jumped so much that the final date was pushed back twice. London's production is still running.

questions.q: Les Misérables is based on a novel by which French writer?
questions.w: Victor Hugo, whose 1862 novel runs to about 1,500 pages.
questions.more: The musical started life as a French concept album in 1980 and was reworked in English by Cameron Mackintosh in 1985, when the London critics savaged it and the public ignored them. It has been seen by more than 130 million people. The famous logo of the waif Cosette is taken from an illustration in an early edition of the novel.

questions.q: The Tony Awards are named after whom?
o: Antoinette Perry, a director and theatre leader
questions.w: Antoinette 'Tony' Perry, co-founder of the American Theatre Wing, who died in 1946; the awards began the next year.
questions.more: Perry had directed Harvey, the comedy about a man and his invisible giant rabbit, and ran canteens for servicemen during the war. The first winners received a scroll and a cigarette lighter or a compact; the medallion came in 1949. Only shows in the 41 Broadway houses are eligible.

questions.q: Which Stephen Sondheim musical is about a barber who takes revenge on London with his razor while his landlady bakes the evidence into pies?
questions.w: Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street, from 1979.
questions.more: The character came from a Victorian penny dreadful and was long believed in London to have been real. Sondheim was so haunted by a stage version he saw that he turned it into a near-opera; it is sung almost all the way through. Tim Burton's 2007 film starred Johnny Depp and Helena Bonham Carter.

questions.q: West Side Story moves which Shakespeare play to the gang-ridden streets of 1950s New York?
questions.w: Romeo and Juliet, with the Jets and the Sharks standing in for the Montagues and Capulets.
questions.more: Jerome Robbins first imagined it as East Side Story, about a Jewish girl and a Catholic boy, in 1949. The 1957 production had music by Leonard Bernstein and lyrics by a 27-year-old Stephen Sondheim, his first Broadway job. Steven Spielberg's 2021 remake won Ariana DeBose an Oscar for Anita, the same role that won Rita Moreno one in 1962.

questions.q: Put these musicals in the order they opened on Broadway, earliest first.
questions.w: Oklahoma! (1943), West Side Story (1957), A Chorus Line (1975), Rent (1996).
questions.more: Oklahoma! is usually called the first modern musical, with every song moving the story along. A Chorus Line was built from taped late-night sessions with real Broadway dancers and held the long-run record until Cats. Rent moved the form downtown, to AIDS, rent strikes and rock.

questions.q: Which musical is built entirely from the songs of ABBA?
questions.w: Mamma Mia!, which opened in London in 1999 and has been seen by more than 65 million people.
questions.more: Benny Andersson and Björn Ulvaeus refused to write new songs or change the lyrics, so the writer Catherine Johnson had to build the plot around them. It is the biggest 'jukebox musical' ever made. The 2008 film, with Meryl Streep singing and Pierce Brosnan trying to, is the highest-grossing musical film in British history.

questions.q: Which composer and lyricist team wrote Oklahoma!, Carousel, South Pacific, The King and I and The Sound of Music?
questions.w: Richard Rodgers and Oscar Hammerstein II, partners from 1943 until Hammerstein's death in 1960.
questions.more: Rodgers had spent 25 years writing with the brilliant, alcoholic Lorenz Hart before Hammerstein. The last song the pair finished was 'Edelweiss', written for The Sound of Music nine months before Hammerstein died; many people assume it is a real Austrian folk song. Rodgers was the first person to win all four EGOT awards.

questions.q: Which 1996 musical, inspired by Puccini's La Bohème, won the Pulitzer Prize after its author died suddenly the night before its first preview?
questions.w: Rent. Jonathan Larson died of an aortic aneurysm at 35, hours after the final dress rehearsal.
questions.more: He had been waiting tables at the Moondance Diner for ten years while writing it. The cast performed the first preview seated at tables, singing it through in his memory. 'Seasons of Love', with its 525,600 minutes, became a standard. Lin-Manuel Miranda directed the film about Larson's earlier years, Tick, Tick... Boom!

questions.q: Which of these shows won the Tony Award for Best Musical? Select all that apply.
questions.w: Hamilton (2016), The Book of Mormon (2011) and Hadestown (2019). Wicked lost to Avenue Q in 2004, and Six lost to A Strange Loop in 2022.
questions.more: Wicked's loss to a puppet show is still called the great Tony upset; Avenue Q's team had campaigned with buttons reading 'Don't Suck'. Hadestown took 13 years to reach Broadway from a tiny Vermont production. Hamilton's 16 nominations remain the record.

questions.q: The Book of Mormon, the 2011 musical about two hapless missionaries in Uganda, was written by the creators of which television series?
questions.w: South Park's Trey Parker and Matt Stone, with Robert Lopez of Avenue Q and later Frozen.
questions.more: Parker and Stone had already made a musical film, Cannibal! The Musical, in college, and said their favourite thing on earth is Rodgers and Hammerstein. The Church of Latter-day Saints responded by buying advertisements in the Playbill reading 'You've seen the play, now read the book'. It won nine Tonys.

questions.q: Which actress originated the role of the green witch Elphaba in Wicked and won the Tony for it?
questions.w: Idina Menzel, with Kristin Chenoweth as Glinda.
questions.more: Menzel had made her name as Maureen in the original Rent and later became the voice of Elsa in Frozen, belting 'Let It Go'. John Travolta introduced her at the 2014 Oscars as 'Adele Dazeem', which briefly made her more famous than the song. Cynthia Erivo played Elphaba in the films.

questions.q: Which musical's 1996 revival is the longest-running American-written show in Broadway history and is still playing?
questions.w: Chicago, the Kander and Ebb show about two murderesses and their showbiz lawyer.
questions.more: The original 1975 production, directed by Bob Fosse, was overshadowed by A Chorus Line and ran only two years. The stripped-down revival, with the band on stage and the cast in black, was meant to run a few weeks. The 2002 film won the Oscar for Best Picture, the first musical to do so since Oliver! in 1968.
